name: Mobills: Budget Planner
price: Free + subscription paywall (Premium required for core features: unlimited transactions/categories, bank sync, web access)
complaints: Cloud sync silently loses entries — users report losing ALL transactions despite app reporting successful sync; support admits 'sync process can get stuck sometimes'
Subscription resentment — users dock stars for sub-only pricing, want one-time fee
Refunds refused for subscribers whose banks turned out to be incompatible (past 7-day window)
Feature parity gaps between Android/iOS (custom recurring expenses missing on iOS)
JustUseApp safety score 10.7/100 across 4,082 analyzed reviews
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium — many free expense trackers exist, but Mobills' 10M users are there for full budget + bill management + sync; free rivals don't cover that. Its Brazilian home market has fewer polished alternatives.
moatNotes: Bank-feed features depend on aggregators (Plaid-equivalents, esp. Brazilian Open Finance) — costly to replicate. But the top complaints (sync data loss, manual budget workflow) are clonable without bank feeds; a reliable manual+CSV clone attacks the pain directly.

name: Expense IQ Money Manager (Handy Apps)
price: Free + premium IAP/subscription ($0.99-$5.99 IAPs; historical lifetime-premium purchases)
complaints: Abandoned — last update July 7, 2023; developer unresponsive, broken website/help pages
Lifetime-premium purchases no longer recognized after reinstall — paid users locked out
Cloud sync/restore unreliable, causing outright data loss
Recurring transactions and bill reminders broken; crashes on new devices/Android versions
10-year users report app simply will not open anymore; support emails ignored
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium — free manual trackers exist, but Expense IQ's base wanted bill reminders + accounts + budgets in one (former EasyMoney users, long-tenure data). Migration pain is the wedge: import their backups.
moatNotes: Pure manual-entry app — no bank-feed/Plaid dependency at all. Cheap to clone; the JTBD (all-in-one ledger + bills + budgets with reliable local backup) is proven by 1.3M installs and paid conversions.

name: Quicken Classic: Companion App
price: Free app, paid-gated — useless without a Quicken Classic desktop subscription (~$60-110/yr)
complaints: Desktop-to-mobile sync chronically broken — 'half of the accounts will not sync', balances don't match desktop
Users report the app lost all their data and stopped syncing entirely
Support unable to fix sync after 1.5-hour sessions
Paying subscribers ($60+/yr) get a companion app rated ~3.0 — strong subscription resentment
freeIncumbentRisk: Low — these are entrenched desktop Quicken users with decades of data; no free product serves 'mobile window into my Quicken file'. Risk is Quicken itself pushing users to its cloud-native Simplifi instead.
moatNotes: Cloning requires reading/syncing Quicken data files (proprietary QDF; QIF/QXF export exists) — a real technical moat but no Plaid cost if you piggyback on Quicken's own downloaded data. Alternative wedge: full local-first Quicken replacement for abandoned desktop-ledger users.

name: Home Budget with Sync (Anishu)
price: $5.99 one-time (full); Lite version free with paywalled limits
installs: 75,000 paid (full) + 100,000+ Lite; below 100K on the paid SKU alone but ~175K+ combined plus large iOS base
complaints: No bug fixes or feature enhancements 'in the last 3 years' per long-time users; developer stopped responding
Notifications never worked on Android
Recurring expense/income features broken on Android
Backup/restore causes data loss; Family Sync between devices unreliable
Household users trapped: multi-device family expense sharing is the core feature and it's decaying
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium-low — 'family/household shared envelope budget with device sync' is poorly served by free apps (Goodbudget paywalls envelopes at 10). Older-user demographic pays one-time gladly.
moatNotes: Manual entry + peer sync — no bank-feed/Plaid cost. Family-sync backend is the only infrastructure needed. Rubric caveat: paid SKU is 75K installs, slightly under the 100K bar; JTBD payment-proof is strong ($5.99 x 75K Android alone).

name: Penzu (journal/diary)
price: Free + Pro subscription $4.99/mo or $19.99/yr (core features paid-gated)
complaints: Paid Pro subscribers not receiving Pro features; only automated support responses
Journal entries lost to app malfunctions; entries not saving even with manual save button
Constant crashes kicking users back to homepage
Double charges, difficulty cancelling subscription, refunds refused
Account recovery/support essentially nonfunctional — users locked out of their own private journals
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium — free journal apps abound (Daybook, Journey free tier), but Penzu's draw is private, password-locked, cloud-synced long-form journaling with email reminders; reliability + data ownership (easy export) is the differentiator users are begging for.
moatNotes: No bank feeds, no third-party data dependency — just solid encrypted sync and export. Low infra cost to clone; trust/data-safety is the sale. Rating sits right at the ~4.1 rubric boundary (AppBrain lifetime 4.11) with recent sentiment worse than lifetime average.

_note: Investigated but rejected (failed rubric): HabitBull (3.6M installs, abandoned Aug 2023, lifetime rating 4.39 — fails ≤4.1 bar), HabitHub (1.3M, abandoned June 2021, 4.30), EveryDollar (4.3), PocketGuard (4.3), AndroMoney (4.6), Spendee (actively maintained), Money Lover/Toshl/YNAB/Journey (no verifiable sub-4.1 Play rating), My Budget Book (~100K dev-wide, healthy ratings).
